Murkowski became dean of [Alaska's congressional delegation](/wiki/Alaska%27s_congressional_delegations "Alaska's congressional delegations") upon Representative [Don Young](/wiki/Don_Young "Don Young")'s death.

Murkowski is the daughter of former U.S. senator and governor of Alaska [Frank Murkowski](/wiki/Frank_Murkowski "Frank Murkowski"). She was appointed to the Senate by her father, who resigned his seat in 2002 to become [Alaska's governor](/wiki/Alaska%27s_governor "Alaska's governor"). Murkowski became the first Alaskan-born member of Congress and completed her father's unexpired Senate term, which ended in January 2005. Before her appointment to the Senate, she had been a member of the [Alaska House of Representatives](/wiki/Alaska_House_of_Representatives "Alaska House of Representatives") since 1999. Murkowski ran for and won a full term in [2004](/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_election_in_Alaska "2004 United States Senate election in Alaska") with 48% of the vote. In 1990 *[Hiten](/wiki/Hiten_(spacecraft) "Hiten (spacecraft)")* – *Hagoromo*,[[281]](#cite_note-294) the first dedicated lunar mission since 1976, reached the Moon's orbit. Sent by Japan, it became the first lunar mission that was not a Soviet Union or U.S. mission.

In 1994, the U.S. dedicated a mission to fly a spacecraft (*[Clementine](/wiki/Clementine_(spacecraft) "Clementine (spacecraft)")*) to the Moon again for the first time since 1973. This mission obtained the first near-global topographic map of the Moon, and the first global [multispectral](/wiki/Multispectral "Multispectral") images of the lunar surface.[[282]](#cite_note-295) In 1998, this was followed by the *[Lunar Prospector](/wiki/Lunar_Prospector "Lunar Prospector")* mission, whose instruments indicated the presence of excess hydrogen at the lunar poles, which is likely to have been caused by the presence of water ice in the upper few meters of the regolith within permanently shadowed craters.[[283]](#cite_note-296)

The next years saw a row of first missions to the Moon by a new group of states actively exploring the Moon.

However, until 1882 he considered the tree to be a form or variety of the Tasmanian black peppermint (*[Eucalyptus amygdalina](/wiki/Eucalyptus_amygdalina "Eucalyptus amygdalina")*) and called it thus,[[11]](#cite_note-Willis67-11) not using the binomial name *Eucalyptus regnans* until the *[Systematic Census of Australian Plants](/wiki/Systematic_Census_of_Australian_Plants "Systematic Census of Australian Plants")* in 1882,[[12]](#cite_note-12) and giving it a formal diagnosis in 1888 in Volume 1 of the *Key to the System of Victorian Plants*, where he describes it as "stupendously tall".[[13]](#cite_note-vonMueller1888-13) Von Mueller did not designate a type specimen, nor did he use the name *Eucalyptus regnans* on his many collections of "White Mountain Ash" at the Melbourne Herbarium. **Honduras**,[[c]](#cite_note-10) officially the **Republic of Honduras**,[[d]](#cite_note-11) is a country in [Central America](/wiki/Central_America "Central America"). It is bordered to the west by [Guatemala](/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala"), to the southwest by [El Salvador](/wiki/El_Salvador "El Salvador"), to the southeast by [Nicaragua](/wiki/Nicaragua "Nicaragua"), to the south by the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") at the [Gulf of Fonseca](/wiki/Gulf_of_Fonseca "Gulf of Fonseca"), and to the north by the [Gulf of Honduras](/wiki/Gulf_of_Honduras "Gulf of Honduras"), a large inlet of the [Caribbean Sea](/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea"). Its [capital](/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") and largest city is [Tegucigalpa](/wiki/Tegucigalpa "Tegucigalpa").

Honduras was home to several important [Mesoamerican](/wiki/Mesoamerica "Mesoamerica") cultures, most notably the [Maya](/wiki/Maya_civilization "Maya civilization"), before [Spanish colonization](/wiki/Spanish_colonization_of_the_Americas "Spanish colonization of the Americas") in the sixteenth century. The Spanish introduced [Catholicism](/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and the now-predominant [Spanish language](/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"), along with numerous customs that have blended with the indigenous culture. Honduras became independent in 1821 and has since been a republic, although it has consistently endured much social strife and political instability, and remains one of the poorest countries in the [Western Hemisphere](/wiki/Western_Hemisphere "Western Hemisphere"). In 1960, the northern part of what was the [Mosquito Coast](/wiki/Mosquito_Coast "Mosquito Coast") was transferred from Nicaragua to Honduras by the [International Court of Justice](/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice").[[8]](#cite_note-auto-12)

The nation's economy is primarily [agricultural](/wiki/Agriculture "Agriculture"), making it especially vulnerable to [natural disasters](/wiki/Natural_disaster "Natural disaster") such as [Hurricane Mitch](/wiki/Hurricane_Mitch "Hurricane Mitch") in 1998.[[9]](#cite_note-:9-13)
